title: Optimization of Immunofluorescent Detection of Bone Marrow Disseminated Tumor Cells
author: Axelrod, Pienta, et al.
materials: For a comprehensive list of reagent vendors and catalog numbers, see Additional file 1: Table S1.

LNCaP prostate cancer cells (ATCC) were maintained in RPMI supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% penicillin/streptomycin. Before spiking into bone marrow, LNCaP cells were seeded with 5 nM R1881 (Sigma, #R0908) in media with charcoal-stripped FBS for two days. Cells were harvested using non-enzymatic cell dissociation buffer (ThermoFisher, #13151014), resuspended in media, washed in PBS, and then counted using the Countess II FL Automated Cell Counter (ThermoFisher). LNCaP cells were spiked into bone marrow at 1000 LNCaP cells per 1.5 million white blood cells (WBCs). Bone marrow was collected from patients following signed written formal consent approved by the Johns Hopkins Office of Human Subjects Research Institutional Review Board.

steps.title: Prepare and Spike LNCaP Cells
steps.instruction: Maintain LNCaP prostate cancer cells (ATCC) in RPMI with 10 % FBS and 1 % penicillin/streptomycin; two days before spiking, seed cells in charcoal‑stripped FBS media containing 5 nM R1881 (Sigma #R0908). Harvest cells with non‑enzymatic cell dissociation buffer (ThermoFisher #13151014), resuspend in media, wash once in PBS, count with a Countess II FL Automated Cell Counter, and spike into patient bone‑marrow samples at a ratio of 1 000 LNCaP cells per 1.5 × 10⁶ white blood cells. Bone‑marrow aspirates are obtained under IRB‑approved consent.

steps.title: Thaw and Fix Plus Slides
steps.instruction: Remove frozen plus slides from storage, thaw at room temperature for 10 min, then fix in 4 % paraformaldehyde for 10 min. Wash slides in PBS for 3 min, followed by two washes in PBST (PBS + 0.1 % Tween‑20) for 3 min each. Proceed to staining starting with the 0.5 % Triton X‑100 permeabilization step.

steps.title: Basic Immunofluorescence Staining
steps.instruction: All steps are performed at room temperature unless otherwise noted. Apply 300 µL of each reagent onto each square of an Adhesion slide and place the slide in a humidity chamber. Rehydrate stored slides sequentially in 70 % ethanol (5 min), 50 % ethanol (5 min), then PBS (10 min). Permeabilize cells with 0.5 % Triton X‑100 in PBS for 20 min. Wash by dipping in fresh PBS three times. Block with 10 % goat serum for 20 min at 37 °C. Decant block and add primary antibodies diluted in 10 % goat serum; incubate 30 min at 37 °C. Wash PBS three times. Incubate with secondary antibodies diluted 1:1000 in PBS for 30 min at 37 °C in the dark. Wash PBS three times. Mount coverslips using DAPI‑containing mounting media and cure overnight in the dark.

steps.title: Treat Adhesion Slides (Rehydration & Wash)
steps.instruction: All steps are performed at room temperature unless otherwise indicated. Apply 300 µL of each reagent onto each square of the Adhesion slide and keep in a humidity chamber. Rehydrate by incubating in 70 % ethanol for 5 min, then 50 % ethanol for 5 min, then PBS for 5 min. Perform thorough washing by placing slides in fresh PBST two times for 3 min each.

steps.title: Optimized Immunofluorescence Staining
steps.instruction: Permeabilize cells on slides with 0.5 % Triton X‑100 in PBS for 20 min. Wash slides twice in PBST and once in PBS. First blocking: apply TrueBlack™ freshly diluted in 70 % ethanol for 1 min, then wash PBS twice and PBST once. Additional blocking: incubate slides in Image‑iT™ FX Signal Enhancer for 30 min, decant, then add 5 % BSA in PBS spiked with human Fc‑receptor blocker (5 µL per 1 × 10⁶ cells) for 30 min. Decant the BSA/FcR solution and apply primary antibody diluted in 5 % BSA; incubate 1 h. Wash PBST three times. Incubate secondary antibodies diluted in PBS for 45 min in the dark (whole‑IgG secondary at 1:2500; F(ab)′ fragment secondary at 1:800). Wash slides in PBST three times, then add DAPI diluted in PBS to 1 mg L⁻¹ for 5 min in the dark. Wash PBST three times, mount coverslips with mounting media lacking DAPI, and cure overnight in the dark.

steps.title: RareCyte Manual Staining of Bone Marrow Smears
steps.instruction: Thaw frozen bone‑marrow smears on plus slides at room temperature for 5–10 min. Fix in 10 % neutral buffered formalin (NBF) for 1 h. Wash slides in TBS twice for 5 min each, then place in PBS. Perform heat‑mediated antigen retrieval by incubating in Tris‑HCl buffer (pH 10) for 6 min at 75 °C, then cool in fresh PBS for 5 min. Wash slides four times with Dako buffer (Dako #K8007) by pipetting buffer onto each slide and decanting. Add Reagent 1 and incubate 30 min; wash Dako buffer four times. Incubate Reagent 2A for 40 min, wash; then incubate Reagent 2B for 40 min, wash. Prepare Reagent 3 freshly spiked with anti‑CD11b‑PE, anti‑CD14‑PE, and anti‑CD34‑PE at 1:200; incubate on slides for 30 min, then perform a final set of washes. Transfer slides to PBS and cover‑slip with RareCyte mountant; let sit overnight at room temperature in the dark.

steps.title: Process Bone Marrow Aspirates and Scan Slides
steps.instruction: Collect three patient bone‑marrow aspirates adjacent to metastatic prostate‑cancer lesions under IRB‑approved consent. Process each aspirate onto plus slides using the RareCyte AccuCyte® system. Stain the slides using either the RareCyte manual staining protocol (Step 6) or the optimized immunofluorescence protocol (Step 5). Scan the same defined region of each slide with the Metafer detection software, using identical scan settings (maximum exposure ≤120 ms, lenient intensity cutoff). After automated gallery generation, manually select populated events to remove non‑green (non‑CK) signals, debris, and double‑positive (CK⁺/WBC⁺) cells as described in the results. Note that scanning of Patient 2 bone‑marrow stained with the RareCyte protocol reached the event limit and required estimation based on scanned area proportion.
